question: Should OpenClaw accept SourceActor as the generic public channel/plugin SDK contract for runtime message-author attribution?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but it promotes a new public context/API shape that future plugins, prompts, and memory integrations may depend on, so automation should not decide the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Approve SourceActor after stack review
options.body: Accept the generic SourceActor object plus scalar mirrors, then land or rebase after the prerequisite Signal mention PRs are settled.

options.title: Narrow the contract first
options.body: Ask the author to reduce or rename fields, roles, or exported types before this becomes a stable SDK surface.

options.title: Reject core SDK surface for now
options.body: Close or park this direction and keep attribution experiments in a plugin or downstream memory integration until a maintainer sponsors a core contract.

recommendation.title: Approve SourceActor after stack review
recommendation.body: Accept the generic SourceActor object plus scalar mirrors, then land or rebase after the prerequisite Signal mention PRs are settled.
